content.title: Sensory Trial | Object, Texture Proof, Reaction, Terminal State
content.summary: Establish expectation by framing the user with the complete object, then prove texture in an independent macro view. Preserve the bodily reaction and recovery action after the first trial, add a second distinct detail, and resolve with both the depleted object and the user's settled state visible.

quick_start.input_format: stable user with complete object + independent macro texture proof + first trial, body reaction, and recovery + distinct second proof + changed terminal object state
quick_start.recommended_input: At a warm lantern night market, an adult traveler in a teal linen shirt shares the frame with a full copper pan of honey-glazed root vegetables. The traveler looks down, glances once at camera, and lifts brass tongs. After one bite, the same traveler chews, exhales through pursed lips, fans their mouth twice, and takes one sip of mint water from a clear cup. Only one glaze trace remains in the copper pan while two small bowls stay in place. The traveler sets down the cup, relaxes, and smiles once toward camera.
required_anchors: Establish one stable user and the complete experience object together before the first trial.
Show one independent close tactile, material or functional proof before relying on the user's reaction.
Add a second proof that uses a different object component, scale or action.
Repeat the opening user-object relation with a visibly changed terminal object state and a settled user.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish expectation by framing the user with the complete object, then prove texture in an independent macro view. Preserve the bodily reaction and recovery action after the first trial, add a second distinct detail, and resolve with both the depleted object and the user's settled state visible.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one stable user and one complete experience object in the same frame. Before showing approval, isolate a tactile, material or functional close-up that visibly proves what the object does. Return to the same user for a complete first-use reaction chain, include one readable reset or relief action, then add a different detail for a second proof. End by repeating the opening relation with a clearly changed terminal object state and a settled user. The mechanism is objective proof to embodied reaction to terminal-state confirmation, not the source person, dish, market or exact food-vlog coverage.

invariants.rule: Establish one stable user and the complete experience object together before the first trial.
invariants.purpose: Defines who is testing what and provides an initial state.
invariants.ablation_failure: Opening on a macro detail alone removes identity and completion context.

invariants.rule: Show one independent close tactile, material or functional proof before relying on the user's reaction.
invariants.purpose: Makes the claim inspectable rather than testimonial.
invariants.ablation_failure: A reaction without object proof can feel staged or unsupported.

invariants.rule: Return to the same user for a complete first-use action, visible physical response and one reset or relief behavior.
invariants.purpose: Turns material evidence into embodied consequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Cutting away before the response or omitting the reset leaves the experience incomplete.

invariants.rule: Add a second proof that uses a different object component, scale or action.
invariants.purpose: Broadens the demonstration and prevents one-gimmick repetition.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeating the first insert at the same scale adds no new evidence.

invariants.rule: Repeat the opening user-object relation with a visibly changed terminal object state and a settled user.
invariants.purpose: Closes the test through before-after evidence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on a bite, hand or isolated smile does not prove what happened to the object.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source young light-skinned woman, beige blouse, hair, facial identity and smartwatch
the source Korean night-market stall, visible Korean signage, plastic drink tower and blue stools
the source red tteokbokki-like skillet, melted cheese, metal chopsticks and exact side dishes
the source exact cheese-pull, hot-mouth fan, drink, second bite and empty-pan coverage
the source handheld food-vlog lens relation, facial reactions, color treatment and any visible marks
